description: The image presents four pie charts comparing the distribution of error types across four different language models — GPT4-o, Gemini1.5-Pro, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct — as evaluated by the FactBench benchmark for factual accuracy. Each chart visually breaks down the proportion of errors attributed to categories such as “Lack of Knowledge,” “Misinformation,” “Safety,” “Ethical Advice,” and “Clarification,” with both absolute counts and percentages labeled within each slice. In GPT4-o, “Lack of Knowledge” dominates at 83.3% (5 instances), with “Safety” accounting for the remaining 16.7% (1 instance). Gemini1.5-Pro shows a more diverse error profile: “Misinformation” is largest at 38.4% (33 instances), followed by “Lack of Knowledge” at 22.1% (19 instances), “Ethical Advice” at 16.3% (14 instances), “Clarification” at 14.0% (12 instances), and “Safety” at 9.3% (8 instances). Llama3.1-70B-Instruct is primarily affected by “Lack of Knowledge” at 75.0% (3 instances), with “Clarification” making up the remaining 25.0% (1 instance). Llama3.1-405B-Instruct exhibits a perfectly balanced split between “Lack of Knowledge” and “Misinformation,” each at 50.0% (2 instances each). The charts use distinct colors for each category and are labeled clearly, allowing for direct comparison of error distributions across models.
